correctness.rationale: Each 113-letter witness window is explicitly checked unique against every reversal. Any admissible finite word yields distinct nonpalindromic four-gram edges in a 64-vertex de Bruijn directed trail, with at most one edge from each of 120 reversal pairs, satisfying a 368-variable, 186-row integral endpoint-flow model. Dropping connectivity is an upper relaxation. The standalone verifier regenerates coefficients, confirms all integer constraints and a primal word assignment, and obtains integer-program minimum cost -110 with the optimization backend reporting matching dual bound -110 and zero gap. This establishes a reproducible solver-dependent finite upper certificate 110 edges = 113 letters. Limitation: a separately formalized, solver-independent rational proof of the upper bound is not included.

value.rationale: The exact finite four-letter four-window maximum is a natural nonbinary counterpart to the recent binary aperiodic maximum problem and is not entailed by the cyclic maximum. It supplies a maximum for open trails that is not implied by any cyclic period construction, and the upper bound is a complete finite extremal optimization rather than a routine choice of parameters. The result is limited to a natural small case and makes no unjustified broader claim.
